classes.note: Elected for five years (Constitution art. 60), earlier on dissolution. Systems: list PR in 31 or 32 circoscrizioni with a national remainder college (1948-1992; the 1953 majority bonus was never triggered); the Mattarellum, 475 single-member colleges plus 155 PR seats (1994-2001); the Porcellum, PR with a majority bonus (2006-2013); the Rosatellum, single-member colleges plus PR lists (2018-), with 12 seats abroad from 2006 (8 from 2022) and 400 seats from 2022.

cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant single-member seat (1994-2005 and 2018-) is filled at a by-election (elezione suppletiva); a list seat passes to the next candidate on the list.

classes.name: Regional elections
classes.note: Counted per region: each regional council election counts once. The 15 ordinary-statute regions' elections since 1970 come from the Interior Ministry's historical archive (Eligendo). Sicily, Sardinia, Aosta Valley, Trentino-Alto Adige, and Friuli-Venezia Giulia elect their councils under their own statutes, and Eligendo doesn't list them; of these, only the Aosta Valley elections since 2003, from the region's own results pages, are counted so far. Neither are four ordinary-statute elections that Eligendo leaves out: Marche in 2020 and 2025 and Molise in 2018 and 2023. The five special-statute regions first voted between 1947 (Sicily) and 1964 (Friuli-Venezia Giulia), the fifteen ordinary ones on 7 June 1970. Trentino-Alto Adige's council has since 2001 been the two provincial councils sitting together, counted under the autonomous provinces. Systems: PR by province (1970-1990), the Tatarellum's PR plus a regional list bonus (1995-), and each region's own law since the 1999 constitutional reform.

classes.name: Presidente della Repubblica
classes.note: Elected by Parliament in joint session with three delegates per region (one for the Aosta Valley) for seven years (Constitution arts. 83 and 85): two-thirds of the assembly on the first three ballots, an absolute majority from the fourth. Each ballot is a contest. Enrico De Nicola was provisional head of state 1946-1948, chosen by the Constituent Assembly.

cadence.administered_by: Parlamento in seduta comune, convened by the President of the Chamber
cadence.vacancy_rule: On death, permanent impediment, or resignation the President of the Senate acts, and a new election is held within 15 days (Constitution art. 86).

access.evidence: ballot-by-ballot votes for every election; the 2013, 2015, and 2022 joint-session records on documenti.camera.it

classes.name: Elezioni suppletive della Camera e del Senato
classes.note: By-elections fill single-member seats that fall vacant: 1994-2005 under the Mattarellum and again from 2018 under the Rosatellum (for example Napoli 2020, Siena 2021, Roma 1 2021, Monza 2023). Before 1994 and 2006-2017 list seats passed to the next candidate.

classes.name: Camera dei deputati del Regno d'Italia
classes.name_en: Chamber of Deputies of the Kingdom of Italy
classes.note: Twenty general elections from 1861 to 1924 (single-member colleges with runoffs, except multi-member scrutinio di lista 1882-1890 and PR 1919-1921, and the Acerbo law's majority prize in 1924), then the plebiscitary single-list ballots of 1929 and 1934; the Chamber was replaced by the unelected Camera dei fasci e delle corporazioni in 1939. The Senate of the Kingdom was appointed. Before 1861, the Kingdom of Sardinia's chamber from 1848 is a predecessor, not this class.

access.evidence: volume I on the electorate and the colleges; volume II's results tables survive as page PDFs at legislature.camera.it/_dati/costituente/documenti/ministerocostituente/

classes.name: Comitati degli italiani all'estero (COMITES)
classes.note: Each consular district's committee of 12 or 18 members (18 above 100,000 Italian citizens) is elected by the Italians registered abroad there for five years (Law 286/2003 arts. 5 and 8), by post since 2015 and only by those who register to vote. The General Council of Italians Abroad (CGIE) is then chosen indirectly by the committees.

classes.name: Presidente della Regione
classes.note: Elected directly, the same day and on the same ballot as the council, unless a regional statute says otherwise (Constitution art. 122 since 1999; from 1995 the head of the winning regional list became president). Sicily from 2001, Friuli-Venezia Giulia from 2003, and Sardinia from 2004 elect theirs directly; the Aosta Valley's president, and Bolzano's, are chosen by the council. One round by plurality, except Tuscany's runoff between the top two when nobody reaches 40 percent.

cadence.runoff_rule: Tuscany only: a second round between the top two candidates when none reaches 40 percent.

classes.name: Consiglio provinciale (elezione di secondo grado)
classes.note: Since Law 56/2014 the province's mayors and municipal councillors elect the council for two years (c. 68-69) by a vote weighted by their comuni's population, on lists of sitting mayors and councillors; Sicily's free consortia held their first such elections on 27 April 2025. Results are posted by each province.

classes.name: Consiglio metropolitano
classes.note: Elected for five years by the mayors and councillors of the metropolitan city's comuni with a weighted vote, and again within 60 days of each new council of the capital (Law 56/2014 c. 21 and 25); the metropolitan mayor is the capital's mayor ex officio (c. 19), so no election.

classes.name: Consiglio comunale
classes.finest_note: comune; polling section in recent Eligendo files
classes.note: Every comune elects its council for five years (four from 1993 to 1999) on one Sunday of the ordinary round between 15 April and 15 June, or the next year's round after an early dissolution, so each comune keeps its own cycle and about a fifth vote each year. Comuni up to 15,000 inhabitants: a single round, two-thirds of the seats to the winning mayor's list; larger ones: a majority bonus to the mayor's coalition. Sicily, Sardinia, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Trentino-Alto Adige, and the Aosta Valley run their own municipal elections.

cadence.administered_by: Ministero dell'Interno through the prefectures (ordinary-statute regions and Sardinia); the region (Sicily, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Trentino-Alto Adige, Aosta Valley)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A council dissolved early (resignations, failure to pass the budget, or infiltration by organized crime) is run by a commissioner until the next ordinary round.

classes.name: Consigli e presidenti di municipio e di circoscrizione
classes.note: Comuni above 250,000 inhabitants, and every metropolitan capital, must divide into districts (TUEL art. 17): Rome's 15 municipi, Milan's 9, Naples' 10, Turin's 8 circoscrizioni, Genoa's 9 municipi, Bologna's 6 quartieri, Florence's 5, Venice's 6 municipalità, and others. Their councils and presidents are elected with the city council; smaller comuni abolished theirs in 2010.

classes.name: Referendum comunali
classes.note: Consultative, abrogative, or proposing referendums each comune may hold under its statute (TUEL art. 8), such as Rome's 2018 referendum on its transit company; held on the municipality's own schedule and published only by the comune.

classes.name: Referendum per il distacco di comuni (art. 132 Cost.)
classes.name_en: Referendums on moving municipalities between regions
classes.note: State-run referendums in the comuni asking to leave one region for another (Constitution art. 132, Law 352/1970 arts. 42-45), such as the Valmarecchia comuni in 2006 and Sappada in 2008; a majority of the electorate must approve, then Parliament decides.

cadence.administered_by: Ministero dell'Interno; the Corte di cassazione's central office

classes.name: Elezioni primarie
classes.disposition_reason: Primaries (the center-left's since 2005, for prime minister, party leader, mayors, and regional presidents) are organized and counted by the parties; no public body administers or certifies them.

classes.name: Consiglio superiore della magistratura
classes.disposition_reason: Two-thirds of its members are elected by the magistrates (a professional ballot) and one-third by Parliament in joint session (Constitution art. 104); neither is a popular election.

classes.name: Consorzi di bonifica
classes.disposition_reason: Their assemblies are elected by the landowners who pay the consortium's levies, voting by contribution class in ballots each consortium runs; they are not public elections.

classes.name: Comunità montane e unioni di comuni
classes.name_en: Mountain communities and unions of municipalities
classes.disposition_reason: Their bodies are made up of members the member comuni's councils designate (TUEL arts. 27 and 32); no vote is held or published.

classes.name: Comun general de Fascia
classes.note: The Ladin community of the Fassa valley in Trentino elects its Procurador directly, with a runoff, and its Consei general by PR; last held 4 May 2025.
